newsitem.title: INDIA: India M&M plans $100 mln industrial park.
newsitem.headline: India M&M plans $100 mln industrial park.

text.p: Indian car maker Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd (M&M) said on Tuesday it will set up a $100 million industrial park in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.

M&M Executive Director Arun Nanda told Reuters the firm had already acquired 1,400 acres (560 hectares) situated about four km (2.5 miles) from the Mahindra Ford auto plant near the state capital Madras.
He said the project -- estimated to cost around $100 million over a period of three years -- would also offer water, power, housing and catering facilities.
Singapore-based Jurong Technologies has begun work on the detailed drawings. The overseas firm will develop a master plan and assist in project management, Nanda said.
"We expect to offer the first plot in the second quarter of 1997," Nanda said.
Auto ancillary makers which are expected to supply components for the firm's automobile joint venture with Ford Motor Company are likely to set up shop at this park.
"But we are not restricting the park to auto component makers," he said.
He said M&M would have a 26 percent equity stake, with state-run Tamil Nadu Development Company (TIDCO) picking up 10 percent.
"The rest will be placed privately," Nanda said.
